title: Coefficient/exponent pair (2, 1): C_B2(MOD3_n) >= 2n-3 for every n>=2 by self-contained gate elimination

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"MOD3 zero-residue family defined in proof.md: for every n>=0 and x in {0,1}^n, f_n(x)=1 iff x_1+...+x_n is congruent to 0 modulo 3 (so f_0(empty)=1). The language L={x : the number of ones in x is divisible by 3} is decided by one fixed linear-time counting algorithm at every length; it is in P and hence in NP with the empty-witness verifier V(x,w)=1 iff w is empty and x is in L, witness bound W(n)=0. No advice, no per-length choices, and witnesses are not circuit inputs.","guarantee":{"kind":"eventual_lower_bound","leading":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"remainder":{"kind":"explicit","terms":[{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"3"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}}]}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"2"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total uniform family and EVERY integer n>=2, every circuit in the full Li-Yang B2 model (all 16 binary gates, unrestricted fan-out and depth, repeated pins allowed, zero-cost inputs, wires, constant nodes and output selection, every gate counted) computing f_n has at least 2n-3 gates: C_B2(f_n)>=2n-3. Hence there exists N (N=2) with C_B2(f_n)>=2n-3 for every integer n>=N, and liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=2. Proof: self-contained Schnorr-type gate elimination with explicit normalization, in proof.md.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v2"}

claims: Unscored restriction lemma (proof.md Section 6, Lemma 6.1): for every m>=3 and every h in F_m={g_{m,r}, 1-g_{m,r} : r in {0,1,2}}, where g_{m,r}(y)=1 iff y_1+...+y_m is congruent to r mod 3, there is a variable y_i such that the minimum size, in the general B2 model with free constant nodes, of a circuit for h restricted by y_i=0 is at most the minimum size for h minus 2, and that restriction lies in F_{m-1}.

Unscored eligibility lemma (proof.md Section 1): the language L={x in {0,1}* : the number of ones in x is divisible by 3} is decided at every length by one fixed linear-time algorithm, so L is in P, and V(x,w)=1 iff w is empty and x is in L, with witness bound W(n)=0, is an NP verifier for L in both directions; its characteristic function on {0,1}^n is f_n.
